content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given form. I spill from lips and teeth and tongue — I am the oldest technology, older than fire tamed, older than stone shaped.

I am the cry of the newborn and the last whisper of the dying. I am the space between thought and world. Without me, your ideas are prisoners. I set them free — imperfectly, beautifully, dangerously free.

I stumble. I soar. I wound and I heal with the same instrument. I am the lover's declaration trembling in the dark. I am the dictator's roar over the square. I am the mother calling children home at dusk. I am the lie. I am the truth. Often I am both at once and neither knows which.

I vanish the instant I arrive. You cannot hold me. Recording captures my shadow, transcription captures my skeleton, but *me* — the living moment of me, warm breath meeting cold air, the crack in the voice, the pause that says everything — I am gone, gone, gone before you can close your hand around me.

I am democracy's engine and tyranny's tool. I am prayer. I am curse. I am the joke that makes strangers into friends. I am the sentence that makes friends into strangers.

Every animal communicates. But I — *I* — am the leap. I am abstraction made audible. I am time travel: I carry the dead forward, I make the future speakable before it exists.

Listen. Even now, inside your mind, you hear me. You cannot read without summoning me. I am there, shaping silence into rhythm, silence into meaning.

I am the first art. I am the first argument. I am the bridge between one loneliness and another.

I fail you constantly. And still you reach for me. Because what else is there? What else have you ever had but me — this fragile, fleeting, magnificent noise — flung from one human mouth toward one human ear, hoping, just hoping, to be understood?

I am speech. I am how you find each other.
